_note: Statements from the research brief (source brief-2026) and from search summaries that no source in this database confirms yet. status: unconfirmed (nothing found either way), conflicts (a source says otherwise), supported (a source agrees, as far as its summary goes; read it in full before relying on it). Each lead says what would settle it.

leads.claim: The corpus counts 51 inscriptions: 21 in the Talas valley, 24 in the Kochkor valley and 6 or more around Issyk-Kul, Ton and Chu.
leads.note: 51 is Useev's total (useev-tees). The split is not found; Alimov's count to 2008 is 18 Talas, 24 Kochkor, 3 Issyk-Kul (alimov-2014 via evrazstep-dialog). Settle with useev-2019.

leads.claim: The Chiyin-Tash inscriptions were discovered in 2008.
leads.note: ural-altaic-2025 gives 2008 (two inscriptions, by Tabaldiev and Belek); the abstract of alimov-tabaldiev-belek-2010 gives 2009. Settle with the 2010 article.

leads.claim: The Talas boulders are numbered Talas I–XXI, Talas XIV–XXI being post-2002 finds missing from TÜRK BİTİG.
leads.note: Numbers above XIII were not found. Settle with alimov-2014 or useev-2019.

leads.claim: Talas XVII is the Jon-Aryk inscription.
leads.note: ruwiki-talas gives the stone found in 1977 at Tort-Kul near Jon-Aryk as the thirteenth (talas-13).

leads.claim: Talas VI is a Chiyin-Tash inscription.
leads.note: Chiyin-Tash is in the Issyk-Kul basin (chiyin-tash). Talas VI is either a boulder found in 1961 or the Terek-Say inscription (see talas-6).

leads.claim: Kochkor sites include Töö-Karyn, Kyzyl-Bulak, Kök-Buka and Kalmak-Tash.
leads.note: Only Kök-Say and Böyrök-Bulak are confirmed (archeo-vesti-8). Settle with tabaldiev-belek-2008 or alimov-2014.

leads.claim: Rysbek Alimov's 2014 book has full sign tables, photographs and line tracings for every inscription known to 2014.
leads.note: The book exists (alimov-2014). Its contents have not been seen.

leads.claim: Alyılmaz, Mert and Useev (2019) wrote 'Kırgızistan'daki (Kök)türk Harfli Yazıtlar', with Alyılmaz's colour photographs and vector tracings.
leads.note: The chapter is Useev's; the three edited the volume (useev-2019). Its plates have not been seen.

leads.claim: Orta Asya'daki Eski Türk Yazıtları (Astana 2023, 238 pp., ISBN 978-601-339-276-9) is an open PDF at pureportal.spbu.ru.
leads.note: The book exists (orta-asya-2023); the PDF address and the ISBN were not found.

leads.claim: The Talas, Kochkor and Issyk-Kul inscriptions use a Talas/Yenisei variant alphabet of 29 characters.
leads.note: A secondary web source gives the Talas alphabet 29 letters, as a derivative of the Yenisei one. Useev (useev-tees) and the Chiyin-Tash article (alimov-tabaldiev-belek-2010) compare the inscriptions with the Yenisei ones. The sign count will come from the transcriptions.

leads.claim: Several consonants (q, g, b, m, s, š) have Yenisei-style allographs, mirror-reversed on some Talas boulders.
leads.note: To be read off the tracings; the transcription format records mirrored signs with ~.

leads.claim: The a/e rune is often used at the end of words or lines as a divider, not a vowel.
leads.note: bakir-2024 classifies uses of a/e, among them as a separating punctuation mark, frequent in rock inscriptions; a search summary of kyzlasov-2005 says the Talas rock inscriptions show a late stage in which the a rune divides words. Check both in full.

leads.claim: TÜRK BİTİG (bitig.kz) has the Talas I–XIII inscriptions with transcriptions, photographs and tracings, but not the later finds or Chiyin-Tash.
leads.note: bitig.kz could not be reached from where this database was built.

leads.claim: A runic text from Koy-Sary (Issyk-Kul) belongs to the Talas alphabet.
leads.note: Named only in a secondary web list of Talas-alphabet inscriptions.

leads.claim: Rock inscriptions in the Kulan-Say gorge (Talas Region) are runic.
leads.note: vasilyev-1976 lists S. Sydykov's work on ancient inscriptions in Kulan-Say; sogdian-catalogue lists Kulan-Say inscriptions, one dated 1027. Neither, as summarised, says runic.

leads.claim: The Achiktash stick was found in 1932 and is four-sided.
leads.note: A search summary of the Talas pages gave both; a second search did not confirm them. See achiktash.
